A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same Sundial research work, with complete main text and appendices A–F. Text comparison and rendering of all 23 pages establish reliable coverage of equations, tables and figures.

before.justification: v3 reports original Sundial forecasting results, training curves, ablations and qualitative predictions in Section 5 and Appendices C–D.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including Sundial benchmark evaluations and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: The architecture, TimeFlow objective and sampling algorithm are unchanged. Correcting the noise dimension after Equation 6 aligns its description with the existing formulation; it does not establish an algorithm or implementation change.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same TimeBench training coverage, six TSLib datasets, 23 GIFT-Eval datasets and 27 FEV datasets. No task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in the benchmark and supplementary comparisons, including Tables 1–3 and 7–9 and Figures 4–5.

E3.justification: Evaluation metrics, splits, model configurations and inference settings remain unchanged, including the prediction lengths, 2880-point context and sampling procedures documented in Appendix B and Table 5.

E4.justification: Sections 5.2–5.6 and Appendices C–D retain the same scaling studies, objective and architecture ablations, calibration analyses, lookback sensitivity tests and qualitative showcases.

E5.justification: Uncertainty reporting is unchanged, including the sampling-based 80% prediction intervals in Appendix D.1. Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seed information or significance testing.

E6.justification: All numerical results and plotted findings are identical, including appendix results. For example, Table 2 reports Sundial MASE 0.673 and CRPS 0.472 in both versions.

T1.justification: After Equation 6 in Section 4.1.3, the initial Gaussian noise y_i^(0) changes from d-dimensional to F-dimensional. This corrects its dimensional definition to match y_i in R^F and their interpolation/subtraction. The equations and derivations otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about native generative forecasting, TimeFlow, trillion-point pre-training, scalability and forecasting performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations of mode collapse and calibration are unchanged. Appendix E retains the same limitations concerning hallucinations, high-frequency data, univariate training and repeated autoregression.

D1.justification: Appendix B and Table 5 retain identical hardware, software, preprocessing and configuration information. Code, model-checkpoint and benchmark access links are unchanged.

R1.justification: Related-work discussions, cited works and positioning relative to earlier forecasting and generative models are identical.

P1.justification: The noise-dimension symbol is corrected in one sentence, and the first-page arXiv version/date stamp is updated. The remaining wording and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: All figures, tables, captions and their placement are unchanged. Rendered differences are confined to the version/date stamp and corrected inline dimension; there is no substantive layout revision.

improvement.justification: v4 makes the TimeFlow formulation more precise by correcting the initial noise dimension to F after Equation 6, removing a local dimensional inconsistency. This is a limited improvement in mathematical clarity; empirical support, reproducibility information, claims and limitations remain unchanged.
